title: Guard regex.match on YAML values with is_string before matching
answers: policy errors on non-string workflow values
github.token detection fails on boolean or number inputs
conftest rule crashes on a with: value
body:
Symptom: The github.token shorthand check misbehaves when a `with:` or `env:` value is not a string (for example a boolean or number from YAML).
Root cause: .github/policy.rego:contains_github_token ran regex.match directly on the raw YAML value.
Fix pattern: Add `is_string(value)` as the first condition before `regex.match` in the helper, so non-string values are skipped.
Constraints: Apply the same guard to any new helper that regex-matches arbitrary YAML values. The PR does not show whether other existing regex checks need it.
applies: Helper predicates in .github/policy.rego that run regex over values taken from workflow or action YAML.
says: The workflow security policy check crashes when a step parameter is a boolean.
Automated pipeline validation errors on numeric values configured in action input fields.
Token compliance scanner fails during pull request checks on non-text workflow inputs.
Support boolean and number environment settings without triggering workflow policy scanner crashes.
Pull request validation breaks when pipeline steps pass true or false values.
search: Helper predicates in .github/policy.rego that evaluate YAML workflow values with regex.match must check is_string(value) first. This prevents contains_github_token from crashing or misbehaving when workflow 'with:' or 'env:' inputs contain booleans or numbers. The guard must be applied to any new helper running regular expressions on arbitrary YAML values.
